inputs.original_text: Lower courts have ruled school can ban wearing such apparel as ‘can reasonably be interpreted as profane’ The case of two Michigan middle-school brothers who were told to remove their hoodies emblazoned with the phrase “Let’s Go Brandon” is headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The siblings are represented by the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression which says the boys’ school violated their First Amendment rights. The phrase was popularized during a 2021 NASCAR event when a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” but the NBC interviewer told racer Brandon Brown they were yelling “Let’s go Brandon!” A judge...
inputs.modified_text: NBC turned “F*** Joe Biden!” into “Let’s go Brandon!”, but schools and courts still decided the cleaned-up version was too dangerous to wear. The two Michigan brothers taking their case to the U.S. Supreme Court are highlighting the real issue: officials decide which political messages are acceptable, and “protecting students” can become an excuse to silence messages they can’t control.
